keep: The idea is named up front: one number scales every area, worked out as ad − bc, with minus as a flip and zero as squashed flat.
The causal step is there: i and j land on the columns, so the square lands on their parallelogram, and evenly spaced grid lines make every square the same parallelogram, so every shape scales alike.
Parallelogram area is earned by cut and slide before the formula, and the formula is earned by boxing [3 1; 1 2] and taking away the corners, 12 − 7 = 5, checked against 3 × 2 − 1 × 1.

Each brief mistake has its own DO screen and hint: dividing to go back (screen 8), the formula without the area (screen 4, no numbers), a negative read as a negative area (screen 10), a minus entry read as a flip (screen 12), the slanted side as height (screen 4).
Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO, ending on two mixed puzzles. Four footnotes, one per sentence, none naming a source. Validator: no problems.
fix: False absolute: 'the height is measured straight up from the base' is only true for a level base. Say at right angles to the base, in explain and practice.
The brief says the parallelogram and shape 'grow', but a determinant below 1 shrinks them and a negative one flips them. Say 'change by the same factor'.

Causal gap in the loop example: 'exactly one pair of currents works' needs its reason in a sentence, that a move which does not squash the plane sends different pairs to different points. The sentence before it is awkward ('no pair might give, or many pairs might').
'Its size is still the scale factor' is vague after a minus sign. Say the number without its minus sign is still the scale factor.
Read-through: screens 5 and 7 animate, so each needs a still and a read sentence that makes sense with no controls.
Explain's stretch and shear paragraph ends on two loose lines after the cut. Put 'the shear keeps every area the same' with the cut, then state the area rule the cut shows.
